Prevention: Remove the remaining fruit from the trees or those that have fallen or that have been attacked after harvest between seasons
Plough the soil around the tree to remove the insect young that live and sleep in the soil
Remove flowering weeds of the same families
Monitoring: Start monitoring one week after the tree has started flowering
Use of light trap for monitoring
Look at the top of the fruit for the presence of the insect and its eggs
Look for the larva and the pupa under the soil around the tree.
Start controlling the problem when you see at least 5 larvae on 10 trees in the orchard
Direct Control: Use trichogramma cards on the trees.
Place them in the middle and on the edges of the field
Use one trichogramma card for ten trees
Calyx cup should be clipped off immediately after pollination as fruit borer lay eggs on calyx cup
Spray neem oil (3%) during flowering stage
Put clean mud (heated by the sun) around the base of the fruit to protect it from the insect
Bag the fruits from an early age to create a barrier to the borer
Restrictions: Use protective clothing when spraying to protect your eyes, mouth and skin
Buy chemicals from a certified dealer and keep them out of the reach of children
Do not eat, drink or smoke during the spray
Diazinon or malathion at 2 ml / litre
Maximum 3 applications per season at intervals of 15 days.
Only use when the fruit is small.
Diazinon can cause severe effects to humans and environment if no care is taken
